page.overview:
What is Currency in Gondor?

The Castar (S. Mirian) was the chief currency used within Gondor. A smaller coin was the tharni (S. canath), a silver coin worth a fourth of the castar.

entity.description:
The Castar (S. Mirian) was the chief currency used within Gondor. A smaller coin was the tharni (S. canath), a silver coin worth a fourth of the castar.

Castar is a Westron word that resembles the word kast in Hobbit-speech and the word kastu in Rohanese, which both mean "mathom". Mirian is a Sindarin word that seems to be derived from mîr ("jewel").

In the 2014 video game , a Castar is the twenty-eighth collectable artifact: the Gondorian Coin. It is found high up on the side of the first ruined tower west of the Haedir in the Fern Outskirts region of the Sea of Núrnen. The Gondorian Coin was a specific Castar, a coin in Gondor, that dated to around the year 2920 of the Third Age. Castars like the Gondorian Coin were widely used by merchants throughout Middle-earth. The Doors of Durin and the great forge of Khazad-dûm featured on the coins in honor of the Dwarves who provided the mithril to make them. The coins became rare relics after Sauron destroyed most of them.
